    sub f { package Z; for our $o (7) { print "o=$o\n" } } f();
    sub g { package Y; for our $p (8) { print "p=", $p, "\n" } } g();
    { package X; for our $q (9) { print "q=$q\n" } }

perl:            o=7 / p=8 / q=9
main and s533b:  o=  / p=  / q=9   -- SILENT WRONG (the loop variable reads empty).

Controls that are RIGHT today: the same loops with no `package` statement before them; the file-level bare-block form (q=9); `for our` at file level after `package Z;`.

SHAPE: a `foreach our VAR` loop inside a SUB BODY after an in-sub `package NAME;` statement.  The loop aliases `$Z::o` (perl: `our` is the declaring package, Z, at the loop head); the body reads a different variable.  Suspects: the requalifier now asks the binder (s533b) -- check what `requalify_home` answers for the loop-head declarator vs the body use (both should be `our` of Z -> the same spelling); or the foreach lowering binds the loop var under one spelling and the body reads another.  First measurement: `./pl2cl` of the one-liner, grep the emitted loop head vs the body read.

Found by probe m1/m4 in the s533 review scratchpad.
